lines:
Advanced ComfyUI integration delivered per aworkit.capability_host.comfyui_integration.

What changed:
- capability-host: new bounded ComfyUI client and API-workflow inspection (endpoint validation, /system_stats, /object_info, /prompt, /history with deadline polling, bounded /view), exported from lib.rs.
- desktop runtime: runtime/comfyui/{settings,bridge,authoring,server,dto}.rs plus runtime/service/comfyui.rs own the persisted `comfyui` Settings section, compilation of the workflow-tool table into the bundled bridge config, tier:balanced parameter authoring with strict JSON + one correction retry + fail-closed binding validation, reachability probe and opt-in local start. Five Tauri commands expose them; ProviderPort gained one bounded tool-free complete_text.
- Python bridge advanced to one typed tool per configured workflow plus comfyui_get_workflow and comfyui_list_node_types, driven by a --config document Aworkit writes.
- Frontend: configuration.ts schema + cross-field validation, settingsV2Port methods, SETTINGS_SECTIONS/sectionFields entry, and a new ComfyUiSection panel wired into SettingsScreen.

Verification:
- cargo check --lib --bins (desktop): clean.
- cargo test -p aworkit-capability-host --lib comfyui: 6 passed.
- cargo test --lib comfyui (desktop): 25 passed.
- python test_bridge.py: "comfyui-bridge: all checks passed".
- pnpm exec tsc --noEmit: clean.
- pnpm exec vitest run src/workbench: 33 files, 300 tests passed.

Environment note: linking the Rust *test* binaries needed TMP/TEMP redirected to the user temp directory, because the MSVC linker otherwise created its temporary file under C:\WINDOWS and failed with LNK1104. No project or system path was modified; `cargo check` and normal builds were unaffected.

Deliver the advanced ComfyUI integration described in the linked specification.

Scope:
1. New persisted Settings section `comfyui` (endpoint, local install path, launch arguments, auto-start, workflow tools with typed parameters and exact node-input bindings, workflow-authoring assistant) plus a dedicated ComfyUI Settings tab.
2. Compile the workflow-tool table into a bundled ComfyUI bridge configuration so each enabled API workflow becomes one agent tool (MCP), reaching the model through the existing frozen tool, approval and evidence paths.
3. Advance the bundled `desktop/tool-plugins/comfyui-bridge` from a generic run tool to per-workflow typed tools plus bounded authoring reads (node type catalog, workflow read).
4. Rust `comfyui` support in `aworkit-capability-host`: bounded HTTP client for `/system_stats`, `/object_info`, `/prompt`, `/history/{id}`, `/view`, base-URL validation, and API-workflow input inspection.
5. Settings action "Auto create parameters": bounded, tool-free model call through the model mapped to `tier:balanced`, strict JSON contract, one correction retry, and fail-closed validation that every parameter binds to a real workflow input.
6. Connection status probe and opt-in local ComfyUI server start with readiness polling and named failure reporting.
7. Tests: Rust unit tests for inspection/validation/authoring parse, Python bridge tests for the dynamic tools, and TypeScript tests for the settings schema and panel.

Reference material: the existing tool-plugin ComfyUI bridge and the Acondi `acondi-creator-tools` autocreate/discovery reference.

Out of scope: release versions and installer bundles.

data.title: Advanced ComfyUI integration: settings tab, workflow tools, LLM parameter authoring, server lifecycle
